features.title: Project directory and the array store
features.user_visible_behavior: A project is a directory on disk that can be created, closed, re-opened in a new process and zipped for a colleague; its arrays survive a restart even though the project list is not yet in a database.
verification: A project directory is created with the documented layout, including arrays/.
An array written and read back in a new process is bit-identical at float32.
The kernels receive float64 - the conversion happens at the store boundary and nowhere else.
The path registry in the user's config directory lists a project that was opened earlier.
Opening a directory that is not a project names what is wrong instead of raising.
No absolute path appears inside a project directory: it is zipped, unpacked elsewhere and opened.
features.evidence: 2026-08-26. On feature/77_project-directory. New module src/chemometrics_workbench/project.py and 30 tests in tests/test_project.py; uv run pytest is 527 passed, 1 skipped (498 before), ruff check and ruff format clean, mypy clean over 30 source files. Layout: project.json plus arrays/, created by create_project and repaired by open_project when a zip has dropped the empty directory. float32/float64: an array written and loaded straight back with numpy.load is float32 on disk, read_array returns float64, and a subprocess - a genuinely new process - reopens the project and reads the array back with a sha256 of its bytes equal to the parent's spectra.astype(float32).astype(float64), so the round trip is bit-identical rather than close. The kernels' own as_float64 is what write_array validates with, so a NaN or a 1-D array is refused at the store with the message it would have been refused with three steps later. Arrays are content-addressed at arrays/<sha256>.npy: writing the same array twice leaves one file and returns the same sha256: hash, which DatasetVersion.content_hash accepts unchanged. Registry: CHEMOMETRICS_CONFIG_HOME, else XDG_CONFIG_HOME, else ~/.config, mirroring datasets.cache_dir; it lists projects most-recently-opened first, once each, keeps listing a directory that has been deleted or unmounted, and a corrupt registry costs a re-open rather than a crash. Diagnostics: a missing directory, a file, a directory with no project.json, invalid JSON, a newer layout_version and an invalid project record each raise ProjectError naming what is wrong - no traceback reaches a caller. Portability: project.json records no absolute path (directory is excluded and supplied by open_project), and a project zipped, unpacked elsewhere and opened with the original deleted returns the same name and the same array. Array paths that are absolute or escape the project directory are refused, which matters because that path arrives from a client over HTTP in #81.
features.notes: Done. Two things deliberately deferred, both to their own issues rather than widened here: the project directory holds only project.json and arrays/ - model artifacts and reports get their directories when something writes one - and there is no locking, so two application instances on one project directory is undefined until 1.3 has a database to arbitrate. Next: #78.

features.title: Reader interface and the CSV/TXT reader
features.user_visible_behavior: A CSV or TXT file imports through a preview that shows what was detected and offers alternatives for every guess, and the corrections the user makes are applied to the imported data.
verification: A European-decimal-comma CSV imports with the right numbers.
A transposed file is detected as transposed, and the alternative orientation is offered.
Wavelength headers, metadata columns and targets are separated, and a correction to any of them changes the committed dataset.
The response validates against the import_preview shape the 1.1 fixture publishes.
The source file's content hash and the reader version are recorded on the DatasetVersion.
A malformed file returns a diagnostic naming what failed, with no traceback.
A real sample file is committed as a fixture.
features.evidence: 2026-08-26. On feature/78_reader-csv. New package src/chemometrics_workbench/readers/ (__init__.py: the interface; delimited.py: CSV/TXT), 34 tests in tests/test_readers_delimited.py, and four real sample files in tests/fixtures/readers/ cut from the committed Tecator dataset with their provenance in a README beside them. uv run pytest is 561 passed, 1 skipped (528 before); ruff check, ruff format --check and mypy over 33 source files all clean. The interface is two functions, sniff and read, plus head: sniff reports a Detection with a Choice for every guess, and read parses the whole file according to a Detection - the one sniff returned or that one with the user's corrections folded in, which is why a correction cannot be displayed and then ignored. Detection, proven against the fixtures: tecator_subset.csv is comma/decimal point/samples in rows with a wavelength_nm axis read off the header; tecator_subset_eu.csv is semicolon/decimal comma with batch as a metadata column and fat and moisture as targets; tecator_transposed.csv is detected as samples_in_columns; spectra_whitespace.txt is whitespace-delimited, headerless, and gets an index axis with a note rather than an invented wavelength range. A descending header reads as wavenumber_cm-1, an unordered header is refused as an axis, and an empty column is discarded with its reason. Corrections are real: read(EUROPEAN) and read(PLAIN) return the same numbers to 1e-4 against load_tecator().spectra[:8, :12], and correcting the decimal separator to '.' on a decimal-comma file fails with a diagnostic instead of silently importing nothing. A correction outside the offered alternatives, and a correction to a field the reader does not offer, are both refused rather than dropped. Diagnostics, never a stack trace: an empty file, a one-column file, a ragged line named by number, a non-numeric cell in a wavelength column named by line, a file of only text, and an unknown suffix each raise ReaderError with a sentence naming what is wrong. Provenance: every Imported carries a SourceFile with sha256: hash, reader name and reader version. The preview payload's keys, and its source, detected, axis and head sub-keys, are asserted field for field against stub/fixtures/import_preview.json, which is the Phase 1.1 contract.
features.notes: Done. Two findings recorded rather than acted on here. (1) A numeric header name settles a column as a variable whatever its cells hold, so one 'n/a' in a wavelength column fails at the parse naming its line instead of quietly reclassifying the column as metadata - the alternative silently imports a dataset one variable short. (2) The axis kind is detected but cannot be corrected: the Phase 1.1 preview shape has no alternatives for it, and adding one is a contract change that belongs to #81 with the frontend finding. Next: #79, or #81 once #79 and #80 land.

features.title: XLSX reader
features.user_visible_behavior: An Excel workbook imports through the same preview as a CSV, including choosing which sheet to read.
verification: A multi-sheet workbook imports, with the sheet chosen in the preview.
A title row above the header, blank leading rows and merged cells do not shift the data.
The same data exported to CSV and imported through #78 gives identical arrays.
The XLSX dependency is declared in [project.dependencies], not borrowed from a development extra.
A real sample workbook is committed as a fixture.
features.evidence: 2026-08-26. On feature/79_reader-xlsx. New src/chemometrics_workbench/readers/xlsx.py and readers/grid.py, 18 tests in tests/test_readers_xlsx.py, and tests/fixtures/readers/tecator_subset.xlsx - the same eight Tecator samples and twelve channels as the CSV fixtures, under a merged title row over a blank row, with a second sheet. uv run pytest is 579 passed, 1 skipped (561 before); ruff and mypy clean over 36 source files. openpyxl is declared in [project.dependencies] and mypy is told it ships no stubs. The interface held, and moved: everything a spreadsheet and a text file share - header detection, orientation, column classification, the axis rules, the read and the preview head - is now readers/grid.py, and delimited.py keeps only what text has (decode, delimiter, splitting, line counting). #78's 34 tests pass unchanged against the refactor, which is the evidence that the move preserved behaviour. Agreement is the sharpest test: read(tecator_subset.xlsx) and read(tecator_subset.csv) give the same values within float, the same sample_ids, the same fat targets, and the same axis to 0.05 nm - the CSV fixture prints its headers to six significant digits where the workbook holds full floats. What only a workbook has: a sheet Choice with the others as alternatives and 'sheet' in correctable; a merged title row and a blank row skipped without shifting the columns; trailing empty rows and columns dropped rather than imported as blank samples; dates rendered as ISO text so a date column is metadata rather than a plausible absorbance; numbers stored as text still put through decimal detection, so '1,5' in a cell is 1.5. Diagnostics: a sheet with no table, an empty sheet, a non-zip file with an .xlsx suffix, and a sheet name that is not there each raise ReaderError naming the workbook and the sheet. A delimiter correction is refused for a workbook, because offering a correction that cannot be applied is the same lie as ignoring one.
features.notes: Done. One interface change landed here and CSV moved with it, as the issue anticipated. Two additions to the shape: Detection.sheet, and Detection.correctable, which is per-reader because a delimiter means nothing to a spreadsheet. A correction that changes which table is read - a sheet, and one day a JCAMP block - triggers a re-detection through the optional resniff hook, because the sample count, the axis and every column classification go stale when the sheet changes. The 1.1 preview screen does not render a sheet chooser, so the correction is reachable through the API and not yet through the UI: that is a contract finding for #81 alongside the file-upload one. Next: #80.

features.title: JCAMP-DX reader
features.user_visible_behavior: A .jdx or .dx file imports through the same preview, with the axis and metadata the file states rather than reconstructed.
verification: A multi-block file imports as multiple samples.
XFACTOR, YFACTOR, FIRSTX, LASTX and NPOINTS are applied - the axis is read, never reconstructed.
A compression form the reader does not support is named in a diagnostic rather than mis-parsed.
The file's own metadata is carried onto the dataset where the model has somewhere to put it.
A real sample file is committed as a fixture.
features.evidence: 2026-08-26. On feature/80_reader-jcamp. New src/chemometrics_workbench/readers/jcamp.py, 25 tests in tests/test_readers_jcamp.py, and two fixtures: tecator_subset.jdx, a LINK block of eight spectra carrying the same eight Tecator samples and twelve channels as the CSV and the workbook, and compressed_forms.jdx, hand-written so SQZ, DIF and DUP can each be asserted against a stated number. uv run pytest is 604 passed, 1 skipped (579 before); ruff and mypy clean over 38 source files. No new dependency: the ASDF decoder is written here. Multi-block: eight blocks become eight samples, each block's ##TITLE becomes its sample id, and the LINK block's own header - ORIGIN, OWNER - is carried onto every spectrum inside it. Blocks whose point counts or axes disagree are refused as two datasets rather than merged. The axis is read: ##FIRSTX, ##LASTX and ##NPOINTS give the values, ##XFACTOR and ##YFACTOR scale them (asserted separately on a file with XFACTOR=2.0 and YFACTOR=0.001), and axis_reconstructed is False. ##XUNITS of 1/CM and NANOMETERS name the axis; MICROMETERS leaves it numbered with a note rather than converted, and a file with no ##FIRSTX is refused with 'does not invent one'. The compressed forms decode: A00 J K then A03 J T gives 100, 101, 103, 104, 104; +10-20+30-40 gives the four PAC values; a0 j J % gives -10, -11, -10, -10. A DIF line's restatement of the previous line's last ordinate is checked, and a file where it disagrees is refused with 'difference form has been misread' - the case that would otherwise yield a plausible spectrum. Refused by name rather than guessed at: a data form this build does not read, a ##PEAK TABLE (a reduction of a spectrum, not a spectrum), an ##NPOINTS that disagrees with the decoded data, a file with no ##LDR entries, a file with headers and no data, an empty file, and a token in no form the reader knows. Nothing in a JCAMP file is a guess, so Detection.correctable is empty and every correction is refused. read(tecator_subset.jdx) and read(tecator_subset.csv) agree within 1e-4, which is three formats and one dataset.
features.notes: Done. The ASDF decoder covers PAC, SQZ, DIF and DUP under (XY..XY) and (X++(Y..Y)). NTUPLES, peak tables and the forms this build does not read are refused by name rather than partially parsed, because a guessed form produces a spectrum that looks right and is not. Two conversions were declined rather than written: MICROMETERS to nanometres, and transmittance to absorbance - both are science the import step should not do silently, and both belong in a pipeline step if they are wanted. Next: #81, which now has all three readers and the array store behind it.

features.title: Import endpoints: preview and commit
features.user_visible_behavior: Importing a file through the running frontend writes a real array into the project directory and a real DatasetVersion that references it; the dataset list is read back from disk after a restart.
verification: POST /api/import/preview returns detections from the reader rather than from a fixture.
POST /api/import commits with the user's corrections applied and writes the array through the store.
The committed dataset is read back from the project directory by a second server process.
The shape is reported as read, which is what the frontend's own envelope check reads.
A file the reader rejects returns the documented error body, not a 500.
The frontend cannot reach these handlers at all: recorded as #99, not worked around.
features.evidence: 2026-08-27. On feature/81_import-endpoints. New module src/chemometrics_workbench/api.py holding the router, a dataset index in project.py (DatasetEntry, read_datasets, add_dataset over datasets.json), and 19 tests in tests/test_api.py; uv run pytest is 644 passed, 1 skipped (625 before), ruff check, ruff format --check and mypy over 42 source files all clean. python-multipart is added to [project.dependencies] - FastAPI's form parser, needed because a file and its corrections arrive together and a browser sends that as multipart. Endpoints, all under the URLs the 1.1 frontend already uses: GET /api/projects and /api/projects/{id} return the one open project, created on first use at CHEMOMETRICS_PROJECT or <config dir>/projects/default; GET /api/projects/{id}/datasets reads datasets.json off disk; POST /api/import/preview returns readers.preview() with every Choice's alternatives; POST /api/import reads with the user's corrections applied, writes the array through #77's store and records a DatasetVersion that references it. Payload shapes are asserted key for key against stub/fixtures/import_preview.json and datasets.json, which is the contract the 1.1 screens render. Proven: a CSV, a workbook and a JCAMP file all preview through the same endpoint and the endpoint never learns which format it holds; a preview commits nothing and leaves no datasets.json; an import writes float32 to arrays/ and returns a sha256: content hash; a second TestClient over a second application - a restart, as far as the server is concerned - lists the dataset back from the directory alone; two imports of the same stem are two datasets with two ids and one name, because a name is not an identity; a correction that cannot be applied (decimal '.' on a decimal-comma file) is a 422 reader_failed rather than a quiet empty import, and a correction the reader does not offer names the field it refused. Refusals are diagnostics: a file of only text is 422 with the reader's own sentence and no traceback, a file with no suffix says no reader claims it, an upload past MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES is 413 before it is written (§4.3 calls localhost a trust boundary), and an upload calling itself '../../project.json' writes into a temporary directory and leaves the project's own file untouched. The temporary directory is empty after both a failed and a successful read. The envelope is reported rather than enforced: §13's limit is computed by the frontend's own states/envelope.ts from n_samples and n_variables, so the honest server behaviour is to report the shape as read - asserted equal between the preview and the committed version - and ?oversize is not replaced by anything. NOT DONE, and raised as #99: the router is not wired into stub/server.py. Wiring it fails 17 of the 40 end-to-end tests, because the fixture pipeline is built on the fixture dataset version and a real import produces a dataset it knows nothing about; and the 1.1 import screen discards the file the user picks and posts an empty body, so it cannot drive these handlers at all. Both belong to #89's one cut.
features.notes: First two stub handlers written for real, behind unchanged URLs, but NOT swapped in: see #99. The swap is one cut in #89 rather than a handler at a time, because projects, datasets, import, pipelines and experiments are one chain in the fixtures. python-multipart is a new runtime dependency, taken because the commit carries a file and its corrections together.

features.title: Drop MSC(reference='supplied') from the schema
features.user_visible_behavior: The inspector no longer offers an MSC reference the executor cannot run; the schema advertises only what a saved pipeline can express.
verification: grep -rn '"supplied"' src/ names only the kernel's own parameter, not models.py.
from_spec no longer carries the branch that raises for it.
The regenerated step_schema.json offers two MSC references, and the inspector's form follows.
The suite is green, including the parity cases.
features.evidence: 2026-08-27. On feature/82_drop-msc-supplied. `MSCStep.reference` is `Literal["mean", "median"]`; the comment above it records why the third option went and what re-adding it would need, so the next person to want it finds the reason at the field rather than in a closed issue. `grep -rn '"supplied"' src/` returns five lines: the kernel's own `MSCReference` literal and its two branches in `MSCTransformer`, plus the models.py comment and the from_spec docstring that both explain the absence - no schema field. `from_spec` lost its `reference_spectrum` parameter entirely rather than keeping a dead argument: the schema can no longer express the case, so there is nothing to pass and nothing to raise about. The kernel call `MSCTransformer("supplied", reference_spectrum=...)` still works and a test asserts it alongside the ValidationError the step now raises - what went is the schema's claim, not the capability. `MSCTransformer`'s error message no longer says the schema carries the choice, because it no longer does. `uv run python stub/generate_fixtures.py` regenerated the fixtures and the only diff is `step_schema.json`'s MSC enum losing `"supplied"`; the pipeline and dataset content hashes are unchanged (sha256:9a684f48..., sha256:e435c053...), which is the check that this narrowed a form and not a number. Green: `uv run pytest` is 603 passed, 1 skipped, including the parity cases; `uv run ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` clean over 58 files; `uv run mypy` clean over 38 source files; `pnpm test` 52 passed with the inspector test now expecting two MSC references; `pnpm e2e` 40 passed, so the inspector's generated form follows the schema without the screen being touched.
features.notes: Open since pull request #22; decided with the maintainer on 2026-08-25. Re-adding it later is additive and needs no migration. Lands before the executor is written against the enum.

features.title: Pipeline executor
features.user_visible_behavior: A pipeline runs from a real dataset: each node's output is computed once, cached on disk, and recomputed only when it or something upstream of it changes.
verification: The pipeline the 1.1 fixture publishes executes end to end and reproduces the fixture's arrays.
Editing one node recomputes it and its descendants, and nothing else.
RangeSelect reads its axis off the DatasetVersion, not off the recipe.
A split branch is fitted on its training rows and the other branches only transform.
A step that fails names the node it failed at.
Moving a node on the canvas does not invalidate a cached result.
features.evidence: 2026-08-27. On feature/83_pipeline-executor. New module src/chemometrics_workbench/executor.py and 22 tests in tests/test_executor.py; uv run pytest is 625 passed, 1 skipped (603 before), ruff check, ruff format --check and mypy over 40 source files all clean. End to end: the pipeline the 1.1 fixture publishes - rebuilt in the test and asserted node for node against pipeline.json, because stub/ is deleted in #89 - runs against Tecator in a real project directory and reproduces every array spectra.json serves except centre_d. The agreement is to 2e-6 on eight nodes and 5e-5 on autoscale_c, and both numbers are measured rather than chosen: the same chain computed in float64 agrees with the fixture to 5.0e-07, which is its 6-decimal rounding, and going through the array store's float32 moves the worst node to 1.3e-06 - except autoscale_c, where a first derivative cancels most of the signal and autoscaling then divides by a small standard deviation, measured at 2.8e-05. centre_d is a deliberate divergence, raised as #97: the fixture fits it on all 240 samples and metrics-and-validation.md §9 requires refitting on the training fold alone. The test computes both, asserts the fixture holds the fit-on-everything number (4.9e-07) and that the executor differs from it by more than 1e-4 (1.2e-03), and then reproduces the executor's own value from fold arithmetic done by hand. Every sample's displayed row comes from the fold that held it out, checked over all 240 rather than on one row. Caching: keys are a merkle chain - a node's own JSON, the source keyed on the dataset version, chained through its inputs' keys - so a second run recomputes nothing, editing branch C's Savitzky-Golay recomputes exactly savgol and autoscale_c, and editing centre_d below the split recomputes only centre_d. A pipeline with a different pipeline_id and name hashes every node identically and reruns nothing, which is what makes moving a node on the canvas safe: layout coordinates live in pipeline_state.json, outside the model the key is taken from. A different dataset version reruns everything. A pruned array file and a corrupt cache.json each cost a recomputation rather than an error. Every node's output is read back out of the store before its successors see it, so a run that hit the cache and a run that recomputed agree bit for bit - checked with assert_array_equal, not allclose. RangeSelect takes its axis off the DatasetVersion: start=900 end=1000 keeps the 51 channels the axis says and nothing about the recipe knows what a nanometre is. Failures name the node: a one-variable window then SNV is "node 'scatter' (snv) failed: SNV with ddof=1 needs more than 1 variables", the same below a split adds "on a training fold of 216 samples", a split below a split, a train_test split with no splitter yet, a version whose array is not the shape it records, and a missing array file are each refused by name. Leave-one-out is the other splitter that works, checked on 8 samples against 8 hand-computed leave-one-out means. Estimator nodes are walked and reported in Run.pending_estimators, not fitted - what a fitted estimator stores is #87's subject.
features.notes: preprocessing.from_spec is the seam and already covers every step the schema can express. The kernels stay pure - no caching or job logic leaks into preprocessing.py. Estimator fitting is deliberately not here: it is #87's subject, and the executor reports estimator nodes in Run.pending_estimators rather than guessing at what a fitted one should store. The fixture's centre_d array cannot be reproduced under metrics-and-validation.md §9 and the divergence is raised as #97.

features.title: Pipeline validator: the two warnings nothing emits
features.user_visible_behavior: A pipeline that will produce an optimistic RMSECV, or a PLS with no centring upstream, warns the user and points at the node - without blocking the run.
verification: A MeanCentre or Autoscale upstream of a split emits the leakage warning, naming the node.
A PLS node with no centring upstream emits its warning, naming the node.
Neither fires on the fixture pipeline.
The warnings do not block a run.
The validate response is computed - the unconditional valid: true is gone.
Each warning states the consequence, not only the rule.
features.evidence: 2026-08-27. On feature/84_pipeline-validator. New module src/chemometrics_workbench/checks.py (check_pipeline, PipelineWarning, two codes), validation_payload in api.py, the stub's validate handler replaced by a call to it, and 21 tests in tests/test_checks.py. uv run pytest is 679 passed, 1 skipped (658 before); ruff check, ruff format --check and mypy over 44 source files all clean; pnpm e2e is 40 passed with the frontend untouched. Warning one, the leak: a MeanCentre or an Autoscale with a split anywhere below it names both nodes and says RMSECV comes out optimistic and that moving the node below the split fits it per fold - the consequence and the remedy, not the rule. Found through intervening nodes, and both splits named when one centring feeds two. Silent when the centring is below the split, when it is on a branch that never reaches one (the fixture's shape - centre_a and split_d are in one pipeline and have nothing to do with each other), and for SNV, Normalise, Savitzky-Golay and the baselines above a split, which estimate nothing across samples. Autoscale counts as centring for both rules because it subtracts the column means before it divides. Warning two: a PLS or PLS-DA node with no MeanCentre or Autoscale anywhere above it says the first component spends itself on the offset and the model carries no intercept to absorb it. Silenced by either kind of centring at any distance above. A PCA with no centring is deliberately not warned about - only pls-regression.md section 3 says 'almost always wrong', and extending it to PCA would be a preference with no document behind it. A PLS fed by a leaky centring is warned about once, not twice: the centring is there, and where it sits is the other warning's subject. Both fire at once on a pipeline that earns both, and neither hides the other. Envelope: the GUESS shape is kept exactly - valid and problems, which the canvas renders by joining the sentences - and warnings is added alongside carrying code, node_id, related and severity, so a canvas can point at the node without parsing a sentence. valid is false whenever there is anything to say, because the 1.1 screen shows the problems only then and reporting valid while holding a warning would drop it. Nothing blocks: check_pipeline is advisory, and a test executes a leaky pipeline to completion after asserting it warns. The stub's handler is computed rather than constant - it parses stub/fixtures/pipeline.json and calls validation_payload - and the fixture pipeline earns neither warning, so the response is byte-identical to the constant it replaced, now for a reason. A third case, MSC above a split, is #103 rather than a widened branch.
features.notes: Both are specified in metrics-and-validation.md section 9 and pls-regression.md section 3 and have never been emitted. The 1.1 handler returns valid: true unconditionally. The envelope keeps valid and problems and adds warnings alongside, so the frontend is unchanged. MSC above a split leaks by the same rule and is raised as #103.

features.title: MSC above a split leaks too, and nothing warns about it
features.user_visible_behavior: A pipeline whose MSC reference is estimated from the held-out spectra as well as the training ones says so, as centring above a split already does.
verification: MSC above a split emits the leakage warning, naming the node and the split.
Its message is in MSC's own terms - the reference spectrum, not the mean.
metrics-and-validation.md section 9's legitimate list says why MSC is not on it.
features.notes: Raised from #84 under its own convention: a third warning becomes an issue rather than a widened branch. MSC estimates a reference from the fit set, so a sample's output depends on which other samples were present - the property that makes centring a leak. SNV, Normalise, Savitzky-Golay, the baselines and RangeSelect were checked and are legitimate above a split; MSC is the only step in the schema that leaks and is not warned about. Open question in the issue: one warning code for all three steps, or a second code, since the sentence differs.

features.title: Real jobs: background execution, progress, cancel and failure

verification: A run submits and returns queued before any work has started.
Progress is counted per node as the DAG walk advances, not interpolated.
A cancelled run stops where it stood and keeps only the nodes that finished.
A run that genuinely fails carries a cause and no traceback, with no affordance.
A 10-fold cross-validated run finishes inside 30 s with progress visible throughout.

features.evidence: 2026-08-27. On feature/85_real-jobs. New module src/chemometrics_workbench/jobs.py (Jobs, Job, JobStatus, Reporter, submit_run) and progress and cancellation hooks on executor.execute (Progress, RunCancelled, node_label); 18 tests in tests/test_jobs.py. uv run pytest is 729 passed, 1 skipped (711 before); ruff check, ruff format --check and mypy over 46 source files all clean. The job suite was run three times over and passed identically each time - it is driven by threading.Event rather than by sleeps, so nothing depends on how fast the machine is. Submission returns before the work starts, as queued with zero progress, which is the honest first frame and the same one the 1.1 fixture opens with. Progress is counted: the executor reports each node as it finishes and the fraction is completed over total, asserted as exactly 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0 over a four-node pipeline with the labels 'Reading the dataset', 'Preprocessing: snv', 'Preprocessing: mean_centre', 'Fitting: pca'. Labels come from the recipe rather than a table of pretty names, which would drift the moment a step is added. Cancellation is cooperative - the executor is asked between nodes - so a node already running finishes and the wait is bounded by the slowest single node rather than by the whole run. A cancelled execution keeps what finished: cancelling after two of four nodes leaves those two cached, and resuming reuses them and computes only the rest. Their values are asserted identical to a run with the cache off, because a node's key is its recipe and its data and never what ran after it. A queued job that has not started is cancelled without waiting for a worker; a running one stops where it stood, keeping the progress it had reached rather than resetting to zero or jumping to one; a late progress report from a node that was already running cannot bring a cancelled job back to life; and cancelling a job that already succeeded leaves its result alone. Failure carries a cause and no traceback - the traceback goes to the log for a developer - and a failure with no message at all falls back to the exception type rather than rendering an empty red box. A job that raises does not take the table with it: the next submission still runs. #49's failed state is reached by a real bad recipe, a one-variable window then SNV, with no ?fail=true. Section 13's budget: a 10-fold cross-validated run over Tecator finishes well inside 30 s and more than two distinct progress values are observed while it does, so progress is visible throughout rather than arriving in one jump. A thread rather than a process, because every kernel operation is NumPy and releases the GIL, and a process pool would buy pre-emptive cancellation at the cost of copying every matrix across a pipe. The envelope keeps the five 1.1 fields and adds node_id beside them, so a canvas can light up the node being worked on and a screen that ignores it renders what it rendered before. Nothing survives a restart, which is Phase 1.3's. NOT DONE: POST /api/experiments/{id}/run is still the stub's. A run needs an experiment, which holds a pipeline snapshot, and there is nowhere to keep one until #89's store - the third feature to reach that cut, and #99 covers it. What the endpoint would do is submit_run, and Job.payload() is what it would return.
features.notes: The 1.1 job envelope is marked GUESS and may change here; a frontend change is the finding. No job survives a restart - persistence is 1.3. The envelope kept its five fields and gained node_id, so the frontend is unchanged after all. The endpoint waits for #89's store, as #99 describes.

features.title: The metrics gap: SEC, SEP, Q-squared and coefficients in original units
features.user_visible_behavior: The four quantities metrics-and-validation.md specifies and Phase 0 never implemented are available and covered by parity.
verification: SEC, SEP and Q-squared are implemented, with RMSEC still dividing by n and the corrections living in SEC and SEP.
Fold aggregation is pooled residuals, not the mean of per-fold RMSEs.
coefficients_original_units back-transforms the foldable chain, and says so when the chain is not foldable.
Each has a parity case against a reference whose aggregation rule is established.

features.evidence: 2026-08-27. On feature/88_metrics-gap. sec, sep and q2 added to validation.py; coefficients_original_units and FOLDABLE added to regression.py; 11 new reference entries and 5 new parity cases; docs/parity-report.md regenerated. uv run pytest is 711 passed, 1 skipped (679 before); ruff check, ruff format --check and mypy over 44 source files all clean. SEC and SEP: bias-corrected scatter, over n-A-1 and n-1. Section 5's identity RMSEP^2 = bias^2 + (n-1)/n * SEP^2 holds to 1e-12, and there is no such identity for RMSEC and SEC because their denominators differ by more than one - both asserted. Their ratio is sqrt((n-1)/(n-A-1)) for A of 0, 3 and 7. Hand arithmetic on a six-sample case where the residuals square to exactly 1 pins all three denominators at once. Adding a constant offset to the predictions moves RMSE and leaves SEC and SEP unchanged, which is the distinction they exist for. n-A-1 <= 0 raises naming both counts rather than falling back to another denominator, as section 5 requires. Q-squared is the same formula as R-squared over held-out predictions and is implemented as such: section 6 puts both denominators on the total sum of squares about the full calibration mean. A constructed two-cluster case pins that - a per-fold mean gives a denominator ten times smaller and a different number, which is what packages disagree on. Negative Q-squared is returned unclipped. coefficients_original_units folds the chain by measuring it rather than restating pls-regression.md section 7's table: every foldable step is affine, so passing the identity through the fitted chain recovers f(e_j) - f(0) and f(0) is the offset. Savitzky-Golay's interp edge handling comes out exactly right with nobody re-deriving it, and a kernel change cannot leave a stale copy here. Proven per step - centring moves the intercept and leaves the coefficients alone, autoscaling divides each by its scale, range selection leaves zeros where variables were dropped, Savitzky-Golay at deriv 0, 1 and 2 - and for a three-step chain, each reproducing the model's own predictions to 1e-10. SNV, MSC and the baselines are refused by type and named. A test shows why that guard is by type and not by probing: SNV refuses a zero row outright, and treating its identity image as a linear map gives predictions more than 1.0 away from the model's own. Parity: 11 entries added, none changed, none removed. q2 against sklearn.metrics.r2_score over scikit-learn's own held-out predictions on the recorded folds - identical within float on all three datasets. coefficients_original_units and intercept_original_units against a PLSRegression fitted on the raw matrix, which reaches the same vector by centring internally - identical on all three, the tecator intercept within rtol 1e-6. A further case asserts the folded model reproduces the pipeline's predictions on the real datasets to 1e-9, which is PROPOSAL.md section 9's CI constraint. SEC and SEP are recorded as unsourced with the reason: neither scikit-learn nor chemotools computes them and mdatools reports RMSE and bias instead, so computing them from another package's predictions would test their model rather than our metric - the standing SNV and MSC had before #13. The report is now 105 comparisons, 105 passed, 0 failed, up from 96. FOUND while generating the reference: scikit-learn's PLSRegression.intercept_ holds ybar, and X @ coef_ + intercept_ does not reproduce its own predict() - out by xbar . coef_, which is 4.79 on tecator against a response range of 0.9 to 58.5. A parity claim built on that attribute would have failed against a correct kernel. The generator recovers the intercept from predict() and asserts it, and pls-regression.md section 14 records the trap. SEC and SEP live in Metrics.extra; the schema needed no change.
features.notes: A Phase 0 inheritance - nothing in #12 verified these. Depends on nothing in 1.2, so it can be picked up whenever the chain is blocked. SNV, MSC and baselines cannot be folded into coefficients; Savitzky-Golay can. The chain is folded by measuring it - the identity through the fitted transformers - rather than by restating section 7's table, so a kernel change cannot leave a stale copy. scikit-learn's PLSRegression.intercept_ is ybar and does not reproduce its own predictions; recorded in pls-regression.md section 14.

(1) Nothing ever wrote experiment.json, so GET /experiments/current - a published endpoint - answered 404 for the life of a project however many runs had happened. executor.experiment_for and jobs.submit_run now write the record on every ending, succeeded, failed and cancelled alike, because a failed experiment is a result and models.py says so on the field. features.evidence:
2026-08-29. On feature/108_pipeline-persistence. `PUT /api/pipelines/{id}` in api.py with a `PipelineWrite` body, `useSavePipeline` and a Save button on the canvas, `withDrafts` in PipelineCanvas.tsx, and a `RequestValidationError` handler in server.py. uv run pytest is 730 passed, 1 skipped (721 before); ruff check, ruff format --check and mypy over 45 files all clean; pnpm typecheck and lint clean; pnpm test 57 passed (52 before); pnpm exec playwright test is **34 passed, 0 skipped** - the three walkthrough tests were test.fixme and are not any more.

THE WHOLE LIST, NOT A PATCH, as decided with the maintainer. One project holds one pipeline and one user edits it, so last-write-wins needs no conflict rules, and the canvas already holds the entire graph it is drawing; a diff would mean inventing an operation language for a problem nobody has. The body carries `nodes` and an optional `name` and nothing else: `pipeline_id`, `project_id` and `created_at` are taken from the stored record, because a client that could send them could rename one pipeline into another. Layout is not in the body either, and deliberately - where a node sits lives in its own file outside `Pipeline.content_hash()`, and folding coordinates into this body would undo #83's guarantee in one line. `test_moving_a_node_cannot_invalidate_a_cache_entry` saves the same recipe twice, which is what a canvas does after a node is dragged, and asserts every node is still complete.

STALENESS STAYS DERIVED, as decided with the maintainer, and nothing here writes a flag. A node's key is its own JSON chained through its inputs' keys, so editing one changes its key and its descendants' and nothing else's; the arrays that no longer match simply stop being found and the node reports `not_run` because it is. `test_editing_a_node_leaves_staleness_derived_from_the_store` runs a four-node pipeline to completion, changes the PCA from 3 components to 2, and asserts source, snv and centre stay complete while only pca goes not_run - then edits snv to an MSC and asserts everything below it goes with it and the source does not. It also asserts the state entry has the keys it always had, so no second record of the same fact was introduced.

NO NEW VALIDATION WAS WRITTEN, because the model already had it. `Pipeline`'s `_valid_dag` enforces unique ids, known inputs, at least one source and no cycles, and `content_hash` covers only `nodes` - so the endpoint constructs a `Pipeline` (rather than `model_copy(update=...)`, which does not re-run validators) and turns ValidationError into the documented 422. One check is the endpoint's own: a source node naming a dataset version the project does not hold is refused where it is written, because the schema would accept it and the run would then fail with nothing to point at.

A SECOND ERROR SHAPE WAS FOUND AND CLOSED. FastAPI answers its own body-validation failures with `{"detail": [...]}` rather than the documented `{"error": {...}}` - a second error format, which is exactly what the envelope exists to prevent, and invisible until a client sends a body that is malformed rather than merely wrong. server.py now handles `RequestValidationError` into the same envelope. It earned its keep immediately: the first end-to-end save failed with "Input tag 'savitzky_golay' found using 'kind' does not match any of the expected tags", naming the field, which is how the step catalogue's wrong discriminator was found in one run rather than by reading the schema. The kind is `savgol`.

THE CANVAS'S DRAFTS BECAME NODES. `DraftStep` carried two display strings and nothing else, because nothing was ever sent anywhere - the step list drew a picture. It now carries the payload the endpoint takes, so what is drawn is what is sent, and the catalogue writes the schema's defaults out rather than leaving them implicit. `withDrafts` chains the drafts onto a terminal node - one nothing else consumes - because that is the only end a list can be appended to; a freshly imported project has exactly one, which is the shape the step list exists for. A branched pipeline has several ends and this takes the first, which is a stated limit: choosing which branch to extend needs somewhere to say so, and that is #51. Ids are derived from the step and de-duplicated against what is already saved, so adding a second SNV gives `snv_2` rather than something the server has to refuse. Five unit tests cover it.

THE EXIT CRITERION PASSES. #50's walkthrough now runs green against the real server: an empty project, an import of a file the test hands to the file input, the detection stated before anything is committed, the dataset opened, SNV + Savitzky-Golay + PCA assembled through the step list, **saved**, **the page reloaded**, and the three nodes still there - then a run that leaves every node complete and a scores plot whose first point and sample id equal what `results/pca` served, to 12 decimal places. The reload is the assertion #108 exists for.

EVERY DIFF TO THE 1.1 WALKTHROUGH, AND WHAT IT SAYS ABOUT THE CONTRACT - which is #90's fourth verification step, recorded here because this is where the edits were made:
  1. `?token=e2e-token&empty` became `?token=e2e-token` against a real empty project. The affordance was a stub's; a state is a fact about a project (#89).
  2. "Use the example file" became `setInputFiles` with a generated CSV. The 1.1 screen discarded the file the user picked (#99); the contract had no way to say which file to import.
  3. Tecator's 240 x 100 became a generated 30 x 12, and the "reconstructed as 100 evenly spaced points" assertion went. That note is `load_tecator`'s, not a reader's: `data/tecator/tecator.txt` carries a prose header and 22 principal components and no reader will take it. A file that states its axis in its header is the ordinary case, and the axis is then read rather than reconstructed.
  4. A Save click and a page reload were added. This is the contract gap itself - #108 - and the reload is what proves it closed.
  5. `results/pca_a` became `results/pca`. The node id is the fixture's in 1.1 and the user's now: `withDrafts` names a node after the step that made it.
  6. The "Queued" assertion became "Done" plus progress at 100. Thirty samples by twelve channels finishes faster than the job poll, so asserting a transient frame would be asserting that the machine is slow. `runs.spec.ts` watches progress advance on a project seeded large enough to see it.
  7. The cancel and failure paths were removed from this file. Both were driven by `?failrun` and both now live in `runs.spec.ts` against a branch that genuinely cannot be fitted, with nothing computed - a real run to cancel and a real failure to read.
  8. The walkthrough got its own server (8768, empty). It imports, so it cannot share a project with anything that also imports.
No new fixture was introduced: the CSV is generated in `e2e/spectra-file.ts` and nothing was committed to make any of it pass.

features.evidence:
2026-08-29. On feature/90_e2e-real-backend. The frontend CI job became a three-platform matrix (ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest, fail-fast false) and **all three are green**, along with check (py3.12) and check (py3.13). Locally: uv run pytest 731 passed, 1 skipped; ruff check, ruff format --check and mypy over 45 files clean; pnpm typecheck, lint clean; pnpm test 57 passed; pnpm exec playwright test 34 passed, 0 skipped, run three times over to confirm it is not flaky.

THE EXIT CRITERION, STEP BY STEP. (1) #50's walkthrough runs green in CI on all three platforms - the step this feature existed to satisfy, and the reason the matrix was built rather than the step amended. (2) The import uses a real file handed to the file input, generated in e2e/spectra-file.ts; no fixture path. (3) The provoked failure is provoked by real means - a PCA asked for twelve components from six channels, refused by decomposition.py in its own words, X-Stub-Fail having gone in #89. (4) Every diff to the 1.1 walkthrough is recorded with what it says about the contract: eight of them, in #108's evidence, where the edits were made. (5) No new fixture was introduced - git diff --diff-filter=A over the branch adds no data file.

THE MATRIX FOUND FOUR REAL BUGS, none of which an ubuntu-only job would ever have shown.

  1. WINDOWS, AND IT WAS THE APPLICATION RATHER THAN THE HARNESS. `data/tecator/tecator.txt` is verified against a checksum pinned in datasets.py before it is read, and git rewrites LF as CRLF on checkout on Windows: every line of the file changes, so its SHA-256 changes, so load_tecator refuses it with 'does not match its pinned checksum'. Anyone cloning this repository on Windows would meet it the moment they touched the reference dataset; it surfaced here as a server that would not start. Fixed with a .gitattributes marking the committed dataset and the reader fixtures `-text`, so what is checked out is what was committed. The check is deliberately not relaxed - a checksum that tolerates a transformation is not checking anything - and test_the_committed_data_is_checked_out_byte_for_byte asserts the outcome on every platform in a second rather than leaving it to a Windows runner.

  2. THE SEED SHUT DOWN THE SERVER'S JOB POOL. Once the seed and the server shared a process (--serve), `with TestClient(app)` ran the application's lifespan, whose shutdown calls JOBS.shutdown() - leaving the server about to start with a dead thread pool and every run failing 'cannot schedule new futures after shutdown'. The seed borrows the import handler; it does not run a server, and no longer pretends to.

  3. A LOCATOR THAT READ THE WRONG ELEMENT, which is what made ubuntu flaky - it failed once and passed twice on the same tree. getByRole('status').first() matched the stale banner rather than the run status bar: both carry role='status' and DOM order puts the banner first, so the locator read whichever the test had just caused. Three spec files now target `.status`.

  4. AN ASSERTION THAT MEASURED THE RUNNER. macOS failed on 'progress advanced through 76, 94' - two sampled frames where the test wanted three, because a quick machine finishes two nodes between polls. #85's claim is that progress is counted from nodes finishing rather than interpolated against a clock, and that is asserted in the Python job tests where it can be observed exactly; here it is enough that it advanced and never went backwards.

HOW THE HARNESS CHANGED TO BE PORTABLE. The seeded projects moved from /tmp to os.tmpdir(); the removal moved from an `rm -rf` in the Playwright command into the seed script as `--fresh`, where shutil does it - a flag rather than the default, because the script deletes a path given on the command line. `playwright install --with-deps` is Linux-only and is split by runner.os. The webServer command is one command rather than two joined by `&&`, and the project directory comes from CHEMOMETRICS_PROJECT rather than the command line, so the seed and the server cannot disagree about which project is open. On a runner Playwright uses the `github` reporter, so a failure is an annotation carrying its message and line rather than an exit code buried in a log; the HTML report and the trace upload beside it, per platform.

WHAT THE DIAGNOSIS COST, AND WHY, recorded because the lesson is cheaper to read than to repeat. Nine CI cycles and three wrong theories - the `&&` chaining, a uv environment race, cmd.exe in general. The cause was that all four smoke steps used `--empty`, and `--empty` never loads Tecator: four diagnostics that each avoided the failing path, and confident reasoning from their passing. The `&&` and uv changes were kept because both are better regardless, but the comments claiming they were the fix were corrected. What ended it was one line of the actual log.
